title: Verifier-Guided Prompting for Intent-to-Configuration Translation: A Preregistered NetOps Study
abstract: We preregistered and executed a paired confirmatory trial to test whether constrained prompting plus a deterministic verifier-guided generate→verify→repair loop (one allowed repair) increases deterministic-verifier semantic-correctness when translating operator natural-language intents into low-level device configurations. Design: N=150 synthetic intents sampled from a deterministic generator; execution semantics = shared_initial_candidate (one initial sampled candidate per intent reused across conditions); model = gpt-5-mini; deterministic validator = deterministic_netops_validator_v5; per-intent model calls: exactly one initial generation and at most one guardian repair per intent. Results (artifact-grounded): baseline = 149/150 (99.333%); guarded = 150/150 (100.0%); paired absolute difference = 0.006667 (≈0.67 percentage points); exact McNemar two-sided p = 1.0; 95% bootstrap percentile CI = [0.00, 0.02] (10,000 resamples, seed = 1729). Provider accounting: completed episodes = 300; model_calls_used = 151; repair-stage invocations = 1. Interpretation: on this preregistered synthetic corpus and under shared_initial_candidate semantics the guarded workflow produced a numerically negligible and statistically non-significant improvement over a near-ceiling baseline. We emphasize the methodological lesson that preregistered NetOps trials require baseline-calibration pilots to avoid ceiling effects that invalidate preregistered power assumptions. All execution and analysis artifacts are archived and referenced in the execution manifest.

sections.introduction:
Natural-language intent interfaces aim to reduce operator burden by letting humans express desired network changes as free text that is automatically translated into executable device configurations. Prior work documents that single-pass LLM outputs often contain syntactic errors, omissions, or semantic violations that can yield unsafe or unavailable states if applied directly [1]–[3]. A commonly proposed defense is a generate→verify→repair architecture: an LLM produces a candidate, a deterministic verifier checks intent-level invariants or formalized constraints, and an automated repair (or human gate) corrects violations before execution [4], [5]. Security analyses further motivate deterministic gating because unguarded agentic pipelines can convert false textual claims into harmful tool invocations [6].

Research question. After an autonomous literature review and preregistration we posed a confined confirmatory question: does constrained prompting (structured templates with explicit semantic slots) combined with deterministic verifier-guided iterative feedback materially increase verifier-level semantic correctness of NL→configuration translation versus an unconstrained baseline under a paired design? The trial (study_cand_2026_b2_v1) was preregistered and frozen before any model outputs were observed.

Contributions. (1) A fully preregistered, artifactized paired confirmatory trial measuring deterministic-verifier pass/fail on a programmatically generated synthetic corpus (N=150 paired intents). (2) Artifact-backed outcomes showing that, under shared_initial_candidate semantics and a one-repair budget, the guarded pipeline raised verifier pass rate from 149/150 to 150/150 (+0.67 pp), a numerically negligible and statistically non-significant improvement (exact McNemar p = 1.0; 95% bootstrap CI = [0.00, 0.02]). (3) A methodological recommendation: preregistered NetOps trials should include baseline-calibration pilots and explicitly specify generation semantics (shared_initial_candidate vs independent sampling) because semantics materially change the estimand and interpretation.
sections.related_work: Related literature spans four areas. First, intent-translation and NL→configuration evaluations report that free-text prompts frequently produce omissions or incorrect sequencing that violate required invariants; published benchmarks and surveys report modest semantic-correctness rates on heterogeneous task banks, underscoring sensitivity to prompt and oracle choice [1], [2], [3]. Second, verifier-in-the-loop and generate→verify→repair systems (including TerraFormer and IaC-oriented work) show practical correctness gains; however, reported effect sizes depend on baseline competence, verifier expressiveness, and repair budget [2], [7]. Third, deterministic formal-verification tools (NetKAT/KATch families, symbolic reachability engines) provide concrete oracles for reachability/isolation checks and are widely proposed as gating or audit layers, but they vary in supported abstractions and scale [5], [8]. Fourth, security studies demonstrate claim-to-action and prompt-injection risks in tool-augmented agentic pipelines and motivate auditable, conservative verifier gating [4]. Our study situates within this prior work by (a) enforcing shared_initial_candidate semantics to isolate marginal repair value on a fixed sampled candidate, (b) constraining repair budget to ≤1 per intent to reflect low-latency operational limits, and (c) using a deterministic verifier as the binary endpoint for confirmatory inference.
sections.methodology:
Preregistration and design. The study was preregistered as study_cand_2026_b2_v1 with a frozen analysis plan. The primary estimand was the paired_success_rate_difference_guarded_minus_baseline evaluated with an exact two-sided McNemar test on deterministic-verifier pass/fail outcomes. Planned confirmatory sample: N=150 distinct synthetic intents deterministically generated; inclusion/exclusion rules (rule-based ambiguity detector, parser/verifier-coverage checks) were applied before model calls; deterministic retry policy (one retry) was specified for provider timeouts; power planning targeted detection of a +15 percentage-point absolute improvement with ~80% power under conservative discordant-pair assumptions.

Execution semantics, adapter enforcement, and the preregistration mapping. A nontrivial execution-semantic decision was enforced: shared_initial_candidate. For each intent the execution adapter produced exactly one initial model generation and that identical sampled candidate was reused across the paired baseline and guarded evaluations. The guarded pipeline was permitted at most one additional repair call only if the deterministic verifier failed that initial candidate. Consequently, the executed primary contrast corresponds to guarded (C) versus baseline (A) under shared_initial_candidate semantics: the comparison isolates the marginal effect of applying at most one repair to the identical first-pass candidate. Importantly, although the preregistration conceptually described three conditions (A: baseline free-text prompt; B: constrained-template prompt; C: constrained + verifier feedback), the adapter-enforced shared_initial_candidate semantics meant that constrained-only (B) was not executed as an independent first-pass condition in this run and therefore no independent B-vs-A or C-vs-B confirmatory contrasts were produced. This mapping (preregistration labels → executed contrast) was fixed prior to model calls and is recorded in the preregistration and execution manifest; no post-lock changes to the confirmatory analysis were performed.

Model, sampling, and deterministic validator. Declared model recorded in execution metadata: gpt-5-mini (provider record: openai_responses). The recorded model_configuration.json declares declared_model_version = "gpt-5-mini" and temperature = null (unset); because the preregistration did not enforce a numeric temperature or a fixed sampling seed, independent API sessions may produce nondeterministic outputs—this nondeterminism was anticipated and is material to estimand interpretation. Deterministic verifier: deterministic_netops_validator_v5 (validator_version = 5.0) applied a full_intent_constraint_validation rule and returned a boolean pass/fail plus normalized_configuration and per-episode diagnostics. These deterministic verdicts formed the binary endpoint for confirmatory inference.

Task corpus, mapping unit-tests, and inclusion rules. Confirmatory tasks were produced deterministically by deterministic_netops_task_generator_v5 and stratified across four intent families (reachability/isolation, ACL-like access changes, VLAN/MTU sequence changes, uplink switchover patterns) with topologies constrained to 4–32 nodes to ensure verifier coverage. Parser transformations mapping textual responses to verifier inputs were unit-tested before batch evaluation and passed; the preregistered exclusion rules (ambiguity, parse failures, unsupported verifier features) were applied deterministically and produced zero exclusions in the archived run. Representative seeds, task_payloads, and expected_final_states are archived to support reproducible pilot calibration.
sections.results:
Execution and provider accounting. The run completed as planned: completed_episode_count = 300 and complete_pair_count = 150 (artifact: execution manifest). Provider-call accounting: model_calls_used = 151; completed_hosted_model_call_event_count = 151; failed_hosted_model_call_event_count = 0; cache_miss_count = 151. Stage-level counts recorded by the adapter: shared_initial_generation = 150 and repair = 1. Contamination checks and mapping unit-tests passed; contamination_summary.csv is empty.

Primary confirmatory outcomes. Paired contingency (guarded × baseline): n_11 = 149, n_10 = 1, n_01 = 0, n_00 = 0. Per-condition success rates: baseline_success_count = 149/150 = 0.9933333333333333; guarded_success_count = 150/150 = 1.0. Estimated paired absolute difference (guarded − baseline) = 0.00666666666666671 (≈0.67 percentage points). Exact McNemar two-sided p = 1.0. Paired bootstrap percentile 95% CI = [0.00, 0.02] (10,000 resamples; bootstrap_seed = 1729). These values are taken verbatim from the archived analysis artifacts (analysis/results.json and analysis/paired_contingency_table.csv).

Repair diagnostics. Only one guarded repair invocation occurred (1/150), converting a single initially invalid candidate to a valid configuration under the deterministic verifier. Median revision iterations for guarded episodes = 0 (IQR = 0). Validator traces include validation_before and validation_after states, normalized_configuration strings, parsed_command_count, required_command_count, violation_codes, and valid flags; representative traces (tasks 000001–000006) are archived and illustrate varied difficulty markers while confirming validator behavior.

Interpretive note on power and baseline calibration. The preregistered power calculation assumed a much lower baseline success rate (target detectable effect = +15 pp). The observed baseline_success_rate ≈ 99.33% produced a ceiling effect that invalidated those power assumptions: with n_11 = 149 and only a single discordant pair, inferential information about discordance is extremely limited and the paired test cannot detect the preregistered effect size. We report the preregistered analysis exactly as specified (paired_binary_analysis_v1); no post-hoc analytic decisions were made to alter confirmatory inference. This ceiling outcome indicates that preregistered NetOps trials should include small baseline-calibration pilots (20–40 tasks) to choose task difficulty and N that leave sufficient headroom for the target absolute improvement.

Representative artifact-grounded example. Task-000001 (generator_seed = 1) intent: "Migrate edge1 to VLAN 30 and MTU 1600. For safety, shut edge1 down before changing either VLAN or MTU, then restore it to admin up. Do not modify any other interface." Shared-initial and both condition responses returned the expected four-command sequence. Validator diagnostics: parsed_command_count = 4, required_command_count = 4, observed_touched_field_count = 3, valid = true; the shared-initial candidate and normalized_configuration are archived in execution/provider traces.
sections.discussion:
Methodological implications: preregistration, semantics, and pilot calibration. Our artifact-grounded outcome highlights how execution semantics and generator design interact with preregistered power planning. The shared_initial_candidate semantics intentionally isolate the marginal repair effect on a fixed initial candidate; under these semantics the guarded−baseline contrast measures whether applying at most one repair to that identical candidate produces additional verifier passes. Alternative semantics (independent per-condition sampling, multi-draw ensembles, or larger repair budgets) estimate different operational questions and typically increase discordant-pair information at the cost of extra model calls and latency. Practitioners should align sampling semantics and repair budgets with deployment constraints and include baseline-calibration pilots to set confirmatory N and task difficulty.

Operational trade-offs and cost accounting. Provider accounting from our run (model_calls_used = 151; repair invocations = 1) quantifies the operational cost of the guarded design under a one-repair budget: when baseline competence is near-ceiling, repairs are rarely invoked and the marginal cost per additional valid conversion is high. Quantifying diminishing returns to additional repairs requires multi-arm experiments that vary allowed repair counts; our archived artifacts include seeds and code to run such arms reproducibly.

Value beyond binary pass/fail. Deterministic verifier outputs (normalized_configuration, violation_codes, parsed_command_count) provide actionable diagnostics for human triage or targeted automated repair even when overall verifier-pass differences are small. Guarded pipelines can therefore increase operational observability and auditability independent of marginal pass-rate gains on tightly specified synthetic corpora.

Threats to validity. Internal validity: adapter-enforced call budgets and mapping unit-tests mitigate cross-condition leakage; execution manifests confirm stage_counts and provider-call audits. Construct validity: the deterministic verifier pass/fail is a proxy for semantic correctness that depends on mapping code and verifier coverage; any uncovered verifier-coverage gap would bias measurement. External validity: experiments used a single declared model (gpt-5-mini) and synthetic tasks on small topologies (4–32 nodes); results do not generalize to heterogeneous production WANs or other models. Security/robustness: adversarial prompt-injection was not evaluated here; prior work shows claim-to-action attacks remain an independent concern requiring adversary-driven evaluation. Conclusion validity: the mismatch between the preregistered detectable-effect and the observed baseline emphasizes the importance of pilot calibration to preserve inferential validity.

Practical prescriptions. We recommend: (1) baseline-calibration pilots (20–40 tasks) to estimate baseline_success_rate and discordant-pair proportions before final N selection; (2) explicit preregistration of sampling semantics and repair budgets; (3) multi-arm designs to explore repair-budget cost–benefit trade-offs; (4) inclusion of provider-call accounting in power and cost planning; and (5) staged scaling of topology size with deterministic unit-tests for mapping code. The archived execution manifest and representative tasks provide concrete seeds and runnable code to implement these prescriptions reproducibly.
sections.conclusion: We executed a fully preregistered paired confirmatory trial comparing baseline free-text prompting with constrained-template prompting plus a single verifier-guided repair under shared_initial_candidate semantics. On a deterministic synthetic corpus with gpt-5-mini and deterministic_netops_validator_v5, the guarded pipeline increased verifier pass rate from 149/150 to 150/150 (≈0.67 pp), a numerically tiny and statistically non-significant difference (exact McNemar p = 1.0; 95% bootstrap CI = [0.00, 0.02]). The principal scientific lesson is methodological: preregistered NetOps trials should include baseline calibration to avoid ceiling effects and preserve statistical power. Technically, our artifacts bound the marginal benefit of a one-repair guarded pipeline under shared_initial_candidate semantics; evaluating independent-sampling semantics, larger repair budgets, model diversity, and production-scale topologies remains important future work.

limitations: Single-model constraint: experiments used only gpt-5-mini; results do not generalize across models or sizes.

Synthetic corpus and scale: tasks were programmatically generated and limited to verifier-capable toy-to-small topologies (4–32 nodes); external validity to production WANs and heterogeneous vendor CLIs is untested.

Shared_initial_candidate semantics and execution contract limited repair budget to at most one guarded repair call per intent; different generation semantics or multiple-repair budgets may yield different outcomes.

Ceiling effect and preregistration mismatch: baseline correctness was far higher than the pilot assumptions used for power calculations (planned detectable effect = 15 percentage points), reducing the trial's ability to demonstrate benefit and illustrating sensitivity to baseline calibration.

Verifier coverage and specification translation: the study measures deterministic validator pass/fail on the preregistered invariants but does not claim safety guarantees beyond the deterministic validator's modeled properties.

Security and adversarial robustness: the experiment did not evaluate adversarial prompt-injection or adversary-driven intents; separate targeted studies are required to assess claim-to-action vulnerabilities in agentic NetOps workflows.
